entries.title: The director behind the action
entries.category: dictionary-labelled Dhaga headword idiom; source-informed editorial reading
entries.literal_meaning: Gobardhan Das, the master of the play.
entries.explanation: The dictionary defines a concealed controller: others visibly act, while this person directs them. The theatrical wording identifies the person behind the action, not a documented theatre practitioner. Our application asks who actually makes a decision when somebody else announces it; hidden direction need not be guessed from appearances alone.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଏମିତି ଜଣେ ସୂତ୍ରଧରଙ୍କୁ ବୁଝାଏ, ଯିଏ ନିଜେ ଚିହ୍ନା ନପଡ଼ି ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ କାମକୁ ଚଳାନ୍ତି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ହେଉଛି—ଖବର ଦେଉଥିବା ଲୋକ ଓ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେଉଥିବା ଲୋକ କିଏ? କେବଳ ଚେହେରା ଦେଖି ଲୁଚା ସୂତ୍ରଧର ଥିବାର ଅନୁମାନ କରିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A named theatrical idiom points to concealed direction behind visible action.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଗରେ କାମ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପଛରେ ଥିବା ସୂତ୍ରଧରକୁ ଏହି ପଦଟି ବୁଝାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ମୀନା ସଭାରେ ନୂଆ ସମୟ ଘୋଷଣା କଲେ। ରବି ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଏହି ସମୟ କିଏ ଠିକ୍ କଲା?” ମୀନା ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତିର ଚିଠି ଦେଖାଇଲେ। / Meena announced a new meeting time. Ravi asked who had chosen it, and she showed him the decision letter. This invented scene explores responsibility; it does not establish a secret plot.
entries.cultural_context: The source labels the whole headword Dhaga and supplies its figurative meaning. Gobardhan Das remains part of the expression; this page does not identify a historical individual, author or origin. Bengali and Hindi equivalents are listed, not evidence of transmission direction.

screened_prior.title: ଜିଭରେ ଘା
screened_prior.snippet: Inability to speak or use the tongue. ହୁଳହୁଳି ବେଳକୁ ଜିଭରେ ଘା, ଖିରି ପୁଳି ବେଳକୁ ପୁଏର ମା—ଢ଼ଗ ୨. ଜିହ୍ୱାରେ ହୋଇଥିବା କ୍ଷତ; ତୁଣ୍ଡଘା — ୨. Sores on the tongue.
